submissions.title: City attorney: Salem data center moratorium means Verrus can't build until it expires
submissions.excerpt: a 120-day moratorium on data center development ... prohibited from approving any data center development regardless of size
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Salem, Oregon city council gave final approval to a 120-day moratorium on all data center development (expiring ~2027-01-19, extendable), while a new city Data Center Task Force studies regulation. The moratorium was prompted by, and directly blocks, a proposed $5.1B AI data center from California developer Verrus at the Mill Creek Corporate Center — that Verrus project is not currently tracked in this database and may be worth adding separately (unverified: I have not independently confirmed the $5.1B figure against a primary Verrus source). submissions.title: Calexico Enacts Permanent Data Center Ban
submissions.excerpt: passed in a 3-0 unanimous decision ... to permanently prohibit the establishment of data centers citywide
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Calexico, California city council voted 3-0 on 2026-09-16 to permanently ban new data centers citywide (adds Article XII to Municipal Code Ch. 17.11; ordinance takes effect 30 days after adoption). Reported as the third California city to enact a full ban, after Monterey Park (June 2026) and Coachella. No tracked project in this database is sited in Calexico, so no projectId is supplied — flagging for the siting/restrictions side of the tracker.
